policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'make haste' renders the imperative of חוש; qere חושה and ketiv חישה are orthographic variants of the same form and the English cannot distinguish them. No note is mapped. Base (qere) fallback retained.

ASV 'hast showed us' renders the 1cp suffix of ketiv הראיתנו; qere הראיתני would be 'showed me', which the mapped textual_variant note 'Another reading is, me' records as the alternative the ASV did not follow in the text.

ASV 'wilt quicken us' renders the 1cp suffix of ketiv תחיינו; qere תחייני would be 'quicken me', which the mapped textual_variant note 'Another reading is, me' records as the alternative the ASV did not follow in the text.
